Posterior predictive checks for a ctsem fit

Source: R/ctStanPostPredict.R
ctPostPredPlots.Rd

Compares data generated from the fitted model against the data it was fitted to, as a set of diagnostic plots. Works for both the stan and julia backends. ctPostPredict and ctStanPostPredict are maintained as aliases.

Usage

ctPostPredPlots(
  fit,
  panels = "all",
  variables = NULL,
  nsamples = NA,
  datarows = "all",
  diffsize = 1,
  interval = 0.95,
  resolution = 100,
  jitter = 0,
  residuals = FALSE,
  timebins = 10,
  lags = 0:5,
  lagcor = TRUE,
  notes = TRUE,
  plot = FALSE,
  wait = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted ctsem model.

panels

Which panels to produce. 'all' (the default), 'structure', 'calibration', or a character vector of panel names (see Details).

variables

Character vector of variable names to restrict to, or NULL for all. 'LogLik' is a valid name here.

nsamples

Integer or NA. Number of generated datasets to compare against. NA uses the datasets the fit carries.

datarows

Integer vector of data rows to use, or 'all'.

diffsize

Integer vector > 0. Lags, in observations, for the rate-of-change panels. One pair of panels is produced per lag.

interval

Numeric in (0,1). Width of the central predictive interval used by the PredictedVsObserved and IntervalCoverage panels.

resolution

Positive integer. Grid resolution of the shaded model density in the bivariate panels.

jitter

Non-negative numeric. Jitter added to the values in the rate-of-change panels, as a proportion of each variable's standard deviation, applied to observed and generated alike. Useful when data are rounded or ordinal. 0, the default, adds none.

residuals

Logical. Include standardised prior residuals as extra variables. Slow, as it needs one Kalman filter pass per generated dataset.

timebins

Positive integer. Number of equal-count bins of time for the MeanTrajectory panel, which shows the mean within each bin.

lags

Non-negative integer vector. Observation lags for the LaggedCovariance panel, passed to ctFitCheckCov.

lagcor

Logical. If TRUE (the default) the LaggedCovariance panel shows correlations, which are usually easier to read; FALSE shows covariances.

notes

Logical. If TRUE (the default), each panel carries a caption saying what it shows and what a departure from its reference line means. Set FALSE for bare plots.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, prints the panels and returns them invisibly. If FALSE (the default) returns the list without printing.

wait

Logical. If TRUE and plot=TRUE, waits for a keypress between panels.

Value

A named list of ggplot objects, invisibly if plot=TRUE.

Details

Two families of panel are produced.

structure panels check whether the model reproduces the shape of the data: Density (marginal distributions), MeanTrajectory (the mean over subjects against time), ValueByTime and ValueByOccasion (the model implied density of each variable against time and against occasion number, with the observed data as points), ChangeByValue and ChangeByTime (rate of change against current value and against time), and LaggedCovariance (the lagged covariance or correlation structure). ChangeByValue is the phase plane. A linear model implies a straight band with a constant slope there, so curvature in the observed points relative to the model shading suggests nonlinear dynamics.

ValueByTime shows where the model expects individual observations, so its band is as wide as the data. MeanTrajectory shows where it expects the mean of a bin of observations, which has a much narrower band, so a bias in the average level is easier to see there.

LaggedCovariance shows ctFitCheckCov as a panel, with one plot per variable, faceted by the variable it is paired with, comparing the empirical values to the central 95% of the generated datasets at each lag. It is the only panel that looks at dependence across time, and so the one most likely to show a wrong drift or diffusion when the marginal distributions match. Call ctFitCheckCov directly to split it by a group or a predictor.

calibration panels check whether the predictive distribution has the right width and location: PredictedVsObserved, IntervalCoverage, PIT, and the PIT split by CalibrationByInterval and CalibrationBySubject. A problem that depends on the time interval points to the dynamics, since the measurement model does not depend on the interval.

The row-wise log likelihood appears in most panels as an extra variable, LogLik, whose distribution should match between model and data like any other. It is left out of the rate-of-change panels. The observed log likelihood is evaluated at the point estimate, so it has no parameter uncertainty, while the generated one does.

SubjectLogLik compares each subject's total log likelihood, as a cumulative distribution across subjects, against the same curve from each generated dataset. This shows subjects the model fits badly over many occasions, which the row-wise panels can miss. The reference is the generated datasets of the same size, so it is valid for any number of subjects.

The comparison is only as precise as the number of generated datasets allows. With few draws the picture is coarse, and the PIT takes only nsamples + 1 distinct values.

See also

ctPostPredData for the underlying table, ctFitCheckCov for the lagged covariance panel on its own, with splits by group or predictor, and ctPhasePortrait for the model-implied phase plane on its own.

Examples

# \donttest{
plots <- ctPostPredPlots(ctstantestfit)
print(plots$PIT)
# }
